extracted.intended_audience: researchers, publishers, editors, reviewers, and other scholarly-communication stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial announcement and perspective on the Peer Review Week 2024 theme 'Innovation and Technology in Peer Review', outlining opportunities, risks, and community priorities for integrating technology (particularly AI) into peer review while safeguarding integrity, inclusivity, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upholding research quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is indispensable to upholding research quality and serves as a platform for researchers, publishers, editors, and other stakeholders to converge, exchange insights, and spotlight advancements in scholarly communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review processes to maintain and elevate research quality through community engagement, shared standards, and ongoing dialogue about best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace innovation and technology to improve peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The critical intersection of cutting-edge technologies and peer review processes should be leveraged to address evolving needs in the academic landscape and foster best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore and adopt appropriate technological innovations that can broaden the reach of peer review and ease adoption of better practices, while continuously evaluating their impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency and workflow automation
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-powered tools and algorithms can boost efficiency by compiling metadata, aiding indexing, automating manuscript screening, and assisting decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy automation where it streamlines workflows and hastens dissemination of scholarly insights, but monitor outcomes (e.g., effects on acceptance/rejection decisions) and avoid blind reliance on automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining transparency, accountability, and ethical standards is paramount when integrating innovation and technology into peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that any technological interventions are transparent to stakeholders, that decision-making processes remain explainable, and that responsibility for outcomes is clearly assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate algorithmic bias
rubrics_metrics.description: There are legitimate concerns about algorithmic bias in AI-driven tools used in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess, monitor, and mitigate sources of bias in algorithms and data sets; validate tools across diverse disciplines and populations before wide deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect data privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Data privacy is a key implication of introducing AI and technology into peer review workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider privacy risks in tool design and deployment, apply appropriate data protection measures, and be clear with stakeholders about data usage and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and augment human expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a risk of displacement of human expertise; it is debatable whether AI will enhance human capabilities and the quality of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI to augment human reviewers (e.g., freeing reviewers to focus on substantive issues rather than formatting), not to replace critical human judgment and domain expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support researchers for whom English is not first language
rubrics_metrics.description: AI may enable researchers and reviewers to focus on substance rather than formatting, particularly those for whom English isn’t a first language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage tools for keyword extraction, abstract composition, and production of plain-language summaries to reduce language/formatting barriers while ensuring content integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote research integrity and DEIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Research integrity and diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) are crucial considerations when discussing innovations in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate innovations with attention to how they affect integrity and inclusivity; aim for multidisciplinary approaches and accessibility to support global research challenges (e.g., UN SDGs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify and broaden the reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can assist in diversifying and broadening the reviewer pool by identifying and recommending qualified reviewers from various fields and backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use technologies thoughtfully to expand reviewer recruitment and reduce gatekeeping, while validating that recommendations produce fair and appropriate reviewer matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and flag ethical issues and inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: AI holds potential as a tool for detecting and flagging ethical issues and inconsistencies in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate automated checks (e.g., for reporting standards or possible misconduct indicators) as part of a broader integrity workflow, with human oversight for interpretation and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated rigor/transparency checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated tools (e.g., SciScore) can help authors, reviewers, and editors assess documents against rigor checks such as NIH criteria, STAR methods, MDAR, and ARRIVE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate validated automated checks to improve reporting quality and rigor; track tool impact on editorial decisions and quality metrics, and collaborate with toolmakers and domain experts to expand coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoughtful, responsible integration and community dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of AI and technology into peer review should be thoughtful, responsible, and driven by ongoing community dialogue and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage the global peer review community in discussions (e.g., Peer Review Week events, polls, and stakeholder input) to share experiences, confront challenges, celebrate achievements, and co-develop best practices and governance.
